# Checklist: security
<!-- Generated by /speckit.checklist -->
<!-- Branch: 006-home-gamificada | Date: 2026-09-16 -->

**This is the most important file of the four.** The feature opens a new anonymous read path over
`perfilMaker`, which carries `dataNascimento`, `vinculoUnesp`, `escolaridade`, `curso`,
`aceiteTermosEm`, `aceiteTermosVersao` and `usuario` — personal data collected under consent at
signup step 2 (feature 004). Principle 5 makes this a security-review surface.

| ID | Check | Dimension | Ref | Status |
|----|-------|-----------|-----|--------|
| CHK021 | **The declaration is collection-wide; the select is per-call.** Once `publicList` is on `perfilMaker`, ANY caller of the public client may `find({ collection: 'perfilMaker' })` and receive the whole row. Is the safe default deny — i.e. should the door REFUSE a `perfilMaker` read that names no `select`, rather than trusting each caller? | [data-protection] | FR-030, FR-031, D2 | [ ] |
| CHK022 | T011 scans the tree for a second caller. Is that a **guard or a convention**? It fails only if somebody writes the call in a form the scan recognises; a dynamic collection name, a helper, or a different formatting passes it. What would make the bound structural instead? | [authorization] | FR-031 | [ ] |
| CHK023 | The day a feature legitimately needs a second public read of `perfilMaker` — a maker profile page, say — what is the intended path? If the answer is "add another select", the exposure grows by one careful author at a time and nothing counts them | [authorization] | FR-031, CLR-007 | [ ] |
| CHK024 | Does `select` defend at the **query** or at the response? Verify against the built SQL, not the returned object: a `select` Payload honours by fetching everything and discarding is a different guarantee, and T007 must be able to tell them apart | [data-protection] | FR-030 | [ ] |
| CHK025 | `depth: 1` populates `avatarRender`. Can depth-1 population pull anything **beyond** the image — the media row's own uploader, a tenant object, a nested relationship — into the anonymous response? | [data-protection] | FR-019, FR-030 | [ ] |
| CHK026 | Does `select` compose with the tenant constraint and the published filter, or can a `select` that omits `tenant` interfere with the `where` the door AND-s in? The clause and the projection are different mechanisms and must not interact | [authorization] | FR-030, D4 | [ ] |
| CHK027 | The personal overlay filters `missaoSubmissao` by the profile resolved from the **session**. Can a signed-in maker of lab A see any row of lab B — and is that confined by the choke point alone, or does the query also need the tenant? | [authorization] | FR-008, FR-030 | [ ] |
| CHK028 | Can a signed-in maker see **another maker's** submission state on the Home? `missaoSubmissao.read` is `scopedAccess()` — lab-wide, not row-owned — so the constraint that makes it personal is the `where`. Is that asserted, and what happens if the `maker` clause is dropped? | [authorization] | FR-008, US1 | [ ] |
| CHK029 | A signed-in visitor with **no profile in this lab** (one login, two labs — CLR-002 of 002): does the band render without percentages, or does the missing profile read as a failure? Both are defensible; only one is specified | [authentication] | FR-008, FR-010 | [ ] |
| CHK030 | **LGPD.** `docs/lgpd.md` records what the product discloses. Making the roster anonymously listable — name, handle, avatar, XP, level, ordered by XP — changes what a visitor can enumerate about a lab's members. Does that document need a line, and does a test bind the document to the code the way `lgpd-doc.test.ts` already does for the erasure list? | [data-protection] | FR-030, FR-031 | [ ] |
| CHK031 | The ranking discloses **relative standing**. A lab with two makers publishes who earned more. Is that intended by the PO decision that made the ranking public, and is there any lab size below which the card should not render? | [data-protection] | CLR-001, FR-017 | [ ] |
| CHK032 | An **erased** maker: CLR-011 of 005 nulls `xpLedger.perfil` and keeps the amount, and the profile row is deleted. Can a deleted maker still appear in the ranking, and does the lab level still count their XP — the two are answered differently on purpose | [data-protection] | FR-017, FR-012 | [ ] |
| CHK033 | `readPublicRanking` runs `overrideAccess: true` on behalf of a caller with no session. Is there any path by which a **caller-supplied** value reaches its `where`, `sort` or `limit`? The signature takes only a limit today; would a future page pass a handle through it? | [input-sanitization] | FR-030, FR-031 | [ ] |
| CHK034 | Field-level read access is bypassed under `overrideAccess: true` (measured in `afterRead/promise.js`). Is that recorded where the next person looks — beside the declaration, not only in the plan — so nobody adds a field rule believing it defends this door? | [data-protection] | D2 | [ ] |
| CHK035 | The `xp-ledger` and `choke-point` isolation layers mutate expressions this feature touches. Does the harness still fail when planted, after `select` is threaded through `buildTenantClient.find`? | [authorization] | FR-030, SC-014 | [ ] |
